text:
sanjay: heads up — saw a new p95 regression on host-side for ~150B token/day tenant after last runtime kernel selector change.

sanjay: flamegraphs point to more time in \`host_parser::emit_chunk\` and a surprising number of small writev syscalls during streaming. KV-cache miss rate up ~3x in the same window.

maria: hmm, did kernel selector fall back to the generic int-path for some models? that often forces different buffer layouts and can break our writev coalesce hints. any commit id?

sanjay: commit f2c9b7d — the selector now prefers the new fused-attn kernel when seq_len<128. regression shows up across seq_len 1..64 requests.

alice: I captured an example HTTP/2 trace — for a single 512B generated chunk we now emit 4 frames (HEADERS + 3 DATA) vs 1 DATA previously. more syscalls + more small writes -> tcp push thrash.

alice: snippet:```
streamer: writev(3) -> 128, 64, 64, 256
old: writev(3) -> 512
```

derek: kvcache behavior could be amplified if the new kernel changes the prefetch pattern (hotspot offset changed). that would inflate cache churn for small requests. can we correlate kvcache key prefixes?

sanjay: yes, key prefix histogram shifted — more misses on the same shard. suspect kernel changes altered per-request proto framing which changes the cache key (we include proto header length).

ops-jen: infra-bot reports a canary rollout at 2024-09-11T03:14:00Z for that commit. infra-bot: canary reached 12% capacity, p95 up ~18% for that shard.

infra-bot: deploy: f2c9b7d -> canary started by @ops-jen. metrics: host_p95_latency +18% (canary), kv_miss_rate +2.9%.

maria: quick mitigation: pin kernel selector to the previous hint for the affected model family and force framer to coalesce small chunks for HTTP/2. should be a small patch.

sam: repro steps I used:
1) start local host runtime with \`RW_KERNEL_HINT=legacy_fused\`
2) run 1k short-chat requests (seq_len 8..64)
3) record writev counts + kvcache hits (prom exporter)

sam: command:```bash
RW_KERNEL_HINT=legacy_fused ./rwinference --models ./models/llama-like --ingress-port 8080
./tools/traffic-gen --qps 300 --seq 8,16,32 --duration 60s
```

derek: if that reduces writev count and kvcache churn we can do an immediate rollback for that model family and follow up with a targeted selector fix.

alice: also add an ingress framer unit test to ensure when total payload < 1k we'll emit single DATA frame. catches regressions early.

sanjay: agreed. timeline: revert canary -> quick patch to selector OR adjust framer coalesce. i'll open a PR with metrics + flamegraph + repro.

maria: tagging perf and runtime to triage: @perf-team @runtime-team :thumbsup:

ops-jen: ping when PR is up and canary plan — i'll hold canary at 0% until we validate.

sanjay: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (WIP) — includes kvcache snapshot, writev histogram and flamegraph in the description.

alice: nice. also add a unit that simulates the kernel layout change so we don't regress framer assumptions in future.

sanjay: will do. thanks all.
